body:
### Summary

The `uv lock` command currently fails if the `.venv` folder / file is not valid (see #19832). It does not seem to require a virtual environment at all since it's possible to run `uv lock` without a `.venv`, wherein it falls back to the global or managed version of python.

Adding the `--active` flag would allow `uv lock` to bypass this error.

Note, this is a temporary solution for #19832.



### Example

In cases where the `.venv` folder has the following structure, it is required to rename to folder temporarily to allow `uv lock` to function.

```
.venv/
|-- 3.10
|-- 3.12
|-- 3.14
```
title: Add `--active` flag for `uv lock`
